name: Camping Baie du Diable
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 46.8375,-75.7045 + operator Pionniers section map: the campground fills the point between Lac Baskatong and its Baie du Diable arm; rows 200-234 back onto the bay shore and the point's rows sit on open sand ~10-30 m from the water, docks along the shore; lakefront

name: Camping au Soleil St-Paulin
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 46.4140,-73.0634: loops and pool west of the Chemin de la Belle-Montagne access road; the Rivière du Loup runs ~250 m east beyond the road and woods; not waterfront

name: Camping St-Édouard
evidence: operator 2024 site plan + satellite (Esri z17) at 46.3273,-73.1402: the park's dammed pond holds an island loop whose traveller 3-service sites Île 1-3 sit at the water's edge (a seasonal row lines the SE shore); main rows ~150 m south; pond

name: Camping la Descente des Femmes
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 48.3879,-70.5894: hillside loops above the Sainte-Rose-du-Nord village; the Saguenay fjord shore is ~200-300 m south beyond the village streets; the small artificial swimming pond ~140 m north is a day-use amenity with no pads confirmed at its edge; default down; not waterfront

name: Camping La Détente
evidence: operator 2025 site plan + satellite (Esri z16/z18) at 45.8567,-72.3667: the NE section's non-seasonal 3-service L-series sites ring a small swimming pond (sandy rim, Salle du lac beside it) on open cleared ground with no treeline or road between; the main seasonal rows are ~300 m SW; pond

name: Camping Lac-aux-Sables
evidence: operator 2024 plan + satellite (Esri z18) at 46.8688,-72.3903: the traveller 3-service LAC row (204-209) faces the village's public natural beach on Lac aux Sables across Rue Ste-Marie (closed to traffic), ~40-60 m from the water; a road and a day-use public beach between = view, not access; lakeview

name: Camping Lac Frontière
evidence: operator 2022 site map + satellite (Esri z17) at 45.0309,-72.0795: the VIP 'bord du lac' RV row L1-L8 sits inside the lake loop road, with the loop lane and a treed strip ~30-50 m between it and Lac Crystal (only tent sites A-G/P6-P7 are at the shore); default down; lakeview

name: Camping Lac et Forêt
evidence: operator 2025 map + satellite (Esri z16/z18) at 46.8413,-72.4927: the loop nearest Lac Croche (section B) sits ~40-60 m from the shore behind a continuous forest band, reached by a path down to the docks; the rest of the park runs SE toward Route 153; not waterfront

name: Camping Lac-des-Plaines
evidence: operator 2022 map + satellite (Esri z17) at 45.80358,-73.81257: the traveller rows run west and south of the small artificial swimming lake, separated from it by the ring road and a wooded strip; the sites on the lake's east side (4-16) are seasonal and two 2-service sites near its SW corner sit across the ring road (no view confirmed); default down; not waterfront

name: Domaine du Lac Libby
evidence: operator site plan + satellite (Esri z18) at 45.2814,-72.3679: the row right behind the docks at Lac Libby's NE corner is seasonal; the traveller 2-service sites 1-6 run up from the swimming beach (baignade) ~40-80 m from the water across the open beach and lawn; day-use beach between = view, not access; lakeview

name: Camping Plage des Sables
evidence: operator 2026 map + satellite (Esri 2026-04-12 20 cm, z18) at 46.1083,-71.9110: the traveller 3-service 50A 'vue panoramique sur le lac' rows overlook the park's man-made swimming lake across its wide sand swimming beach (~20-40 m of used day-use beach between pads and water); view, not access; lakeview

name: Camping du Parc
evidence: operator map + satellite (Esri z17/z18) at 46.6012,-72.8463: the small swimming pond (Lac des Iris) is ringed by trees on its north and west shores and by its swimming beach and the Chemin des Berges lane on the south/east, with the RV rows behind the lane and treeline (the few sites drawn at its NW tip are not confirmed open to the water); the Rivière Shawinigan is across Route 351; default down; not waterfront

name: Camping Saint-Boniface
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 46.52635,-72.80679: small loops around the pool and red-roof building north of Boulevard Trudel Est (Route 153); the only water is a creek in the wooded ravine ~250 m north; not waterfront

name: Camping Vallée Bleue Resort
evidence: operator site plan + satellite (Esri z17) at 45.19800,-72.68439: the shore row (499-515) sits between the Bord de l'Eau lane and the park's lake, pads ~10-20 m from the water with nothing between; its traveller 3-service 30A sites 510-515 are on that row; lakefront

name: Camping Causapscal chez Moose
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 48.37336,-67.23899: terraced loops and pool on the hillside NE of Route 132 at Causapscal; no river or lake in the frame (the Matapédia is beyond the highway and woods); not waterfront

name: Camping Aventure Rivière-Noire
evidence: satellite (Esri z18) at 46.3098,-73.5856: the west row of RV pads sits ~10-30 m from a ~60-80 m wide reach of the Rivière Noire on open ground with scattered conifers, no road between (Route 131's embankment is on the far bank); the operator sells these as riverside 2-service sites; riverfront

name: Domaine de l'Ange-Gardien
evidence: operator site map + satellite (Esri z17) at 45.57070,-75.51416: wooded loops north of the reception building; the small central pond (étang) sits inside a used green (horseshoe pits, playground) ringed by the site lanes, and the swimming lake by the entrance has no RV sites beside it; default down; not waterfront

name: Camping Soleil
evidence: operator map + satellite (Esri z18) at 46.2222,-71.3842: the traveller 2-service rows (J, T, A) run along the east side of the park, but a continuous wooded riparian strip ~15-25 m wide separates the pads from the narrow, canopy-covered Rivière Osgood and its tributary; default down; not waterfront

name: Camping écologique de Frelighsburg
evidence: operator 2024 plan + satellite (Esri z18) at 45.0206,-72.8275: the riverside sites 9-62 line the west bank of the Rivière aux Brochets, pads ~10-20 m from the water among scattered trees, with a footbridge across; the channel measures ~20 m here (under ~30 m = creekside); creekside

name: Camping des Étoiles
evidence: satellite (Esri z16/z18) at 48.0437,-65.1675: the park is a strip of loops running from Route 132 down to the low bluff over the Baie des Chaleurs; the southern loops and the units along the east edge look across open grass to the bay ~50-150 m away, beyond a shrubby bluff edge and a narrow beach (climb-down, not walk-across); bayview

name: Camping Larochelle
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 46.43360,-72.62922: dense rows and a pull-through loop NW of Rue des Marguerites in the sandy pine plain north of Trois-Rivières; no lake or river in the frame; not waterfront

name: Camping La Pinède
evidence: operator site plan + satellite (Esri z18) at 45.8846,-75.0842: the traveller 2-service fan (red on the plan) and the shore row sit ~10-30 m from the wide channel the operator labels 'Rivière' (~250 m across, with an island) on open ground, docks and boats at the bank and a sandy beach at the point; riverfront

name: Camping Horizon
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 45.82232,-73.63179: dense rows and a pool beside a residential street grid in farmland; no lake or river in the frame; not waterfront

name: Camping Oasis
evidence: operator 2023 plan + satellite (Esri z17/z18) at 45.4694,-72.8135: the traveller 3-service column 505-518 lines the outer side of the Avenue Tour du Lac lane around the park's small swimming lake, ~20-30 m from the water across the lane and its open grass bank (view, lane between); the main block is north; lakeview

name: Camping du Rivage
evidence: satellite (Esri z18) at 49.12514,-66.53641: RV pads on the open grass/dune strip on the beach side of 1re Avenue Ouest at Sainte-Anne-des-Monts, with nothing between them and the open sand beach on the St. Lawrence estuary: ~25 m to the high-water wrack line, ~50 m to the water at the time of the image (street behind the sites, landward); bayfront

name: Camping Beau-Soleil
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 45.6688,-71.5228: open traveller pull-through loops and the seasonal rows north of the highway; the small on-site ponds lie ~100 m south-west near the highway with no pads at their edge; not waterfront

name: Camping de la Demi-Lieue
evidence: satellite (Esri z17/z18) at 47.2466,-70.2367: the St. Lawrence frontage is a wide rocky tidal flat below a wooded bank; most rows sit behind a continuous shore treeline, but the lane along the top of the bank at the NE end (where the operator sells 2-service 'bord du fleuve' sites) has only scattered trees and overlooks the flats ~20-40 m away across the bank (climb-down, not walk-across); riverview

name: Camping du Gouffre
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 47.4904,-70.5122: the campground fills the inside of a bend of the Rivière du Gouffre (~40-60 m wide); the pads on the point sit ~10-30 m from the bank on open sand and grass with scattered trees and nothing between; riverfront

name: Domaine des Érables
evidence: Parkbridge 2026 resort map + satellite (Esri z17) at 45.89943,-73.15743: the Voyageur rows 1401-1426 sit between their lane and the west bank of the park's ~300 m trout-fishing pond (Lac de pêche à la truite), pads ~10-20 m from the water on open grass; the Richelieu River is east beyond Rue St-Pierre and the houses; pond

name: Camping Domaine Ensoleillé 2000
evidence: satellite (Esri z17) at 49.48545,-67.23279: loops on a terrace east of Route 138 above a tidal bay of the St. Lawrence at Îlets-Caribou; the east rows (the operator's panoramic sites) overlook the bay's flats across a shrubby bank ~20-40 m wide (bench above, climb-down); bayview

name: Camping Sainte-Madeleine
evidence: operator 2024 per-site plan + satellite (Esri z17/z18) at 45.6037,-73.1036: the narrow Rivière Huron runs through the park under full canopy (satellite cannot resolve it), and the per-site plan draws rows 101-113 and the 2-service 30A rows 60-69 backing directly onto it; creek-sized stream; creekside

name: Camping 2 Rivières
evidence: satellite (Esri z18) at 45.7959,-70.6346: the park's east rows line a lane ~10-25 m from the ~40-60 m wide rocky river north-west of the Route 204 bridge, behind a partial riparian treeline (view through gaps, not open access); the western rows (mostly empty in a May 2020 pre-opening frame, likely the traveller section) are away from the water; riverview

name: Camping de la Mine de Cuivre
evidence: operator site plan + satellite (Esri z17/z18) at 45.2915,-72.3207: the rows on the north side of the park's ~100 m pond (l'Étang) sit across the shore lane and a sandy strip ~15-40 m from the water; the SE rows near the outlet are partly screened by trees; the creek on the far side runs through wetland away from the loops; view with a lane between; lakeview

name: Camping au Soleil St-Côme
evidence: operator 2026 plan + satellite (Esri z18) at 46.2846,-73.7952: the loops run NE from Rang Versailles under pines; the Rivière L'Assomption lies ~40-60 m beyond the north-east rows through forest, reached by the plan's 'accès à la rivière' path (access, not frontage); default down; not waterfront

name: Domaine Parc Estrie (Parkbridge)
evidence: Parkbridge resort map + satellite (Esri z17) at 45.2924,-72.1016: a dense grid of rows on the south side of Magog; only small ornamental ponds near the entrance and treatment basins to the south, no pads on any water; Lac Memphrémagog is in town, not at the park; not waterfront

name: Camping Union Parc de la Chaudière
evidence: satellite (Esri z18) at 46.5259,-71.1124: the riverside row (the operator's separately priced 3-service 'bord de l'eau' sites) sits ~10-20 m from the ~150 m wide Chaudière River on the top of a rocky, walkable bank, with only a thin broken line of trees between; riverfront

name: Camping de l'Estrie
evidence: operator 2026 site map + satellite (Esri z18) at 45.3301,-72.4842: the 3-service lakeside sites (3-8, sold as 'bord du lac') and the neighbouring rows sit ~10-25 m from Lac aux Canards, a ~120 m pond on the park's north side, on open ground with nothing between; dock on the east shore; pond

name: Camping des Chutes Hunter
evidence: satellite (Esri z17/z18) at 45.0647,-72.8747: open rows west of a sandy beach area holding a small, murky swimming pond, wooded loops north and a creek ravine (the Hunter falls) in the forest to the south-east; no pads confirmed at any water's edge (the 'Lac' sites are not resolvable as frontage); default down; not waterfront

name: Camping La Gervaisie
evidence: operator 2025 plan + satellite (Esri z17) at 46.77153,-72.55324: the rows sit north of Chemin du Lac Trottier behind a tree-lined boundary; the road and the campground's beach/day-use lawn lie between them and Lac Trottier ~50-80 m away; default down; not waterfront
